title: Portland, the changeover
logline: The Portland station where she changed buses, drawn from nothing: a big room, a clock, a bank of seats bolted together, a coffee stand closed. He never saw it. He gets the clock wrong on purpose.

panels.composition: A bus station's waiting room, large, fluorescent, a bank of bolted seats, a wall clock, a closed coffee stand with its shutter down. The clock's hands drawn at an impossible angle — both pointing at the same number.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a large fluorescent bus-station waiting room with bolted rows of seats and a closed coffee stand and a wall clock whose hands both point at the same number, no people, no words
image.notes: The clock's hands overlap: a place drawn from nothing has a tell.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Drawn from nothing. The clock is the tell.
